short_cite: WISE Uranium chronology of major tailings dam failures
full_citation: WISE Uranium Project (continuing). Chronology of major tailings dam accidents (from 1960 to date). Compiled by Peter Diehl. Accessed 2026-10-22.
notes: NGO compilation; one row per failure with date, operator/commodity, volume, cause. Used for volumes of E001, E003, E005-E007, E009-E010, E012, E014-E015, E017-E021. Secondary: figures are as reported by press and operators; volumes mix slurry and water. Page is long; read in two 100,000-character chunks. WISE gives Dan River as 74,400 t ash; Duke later revised to 30,000-39,000 short tons.

short_cite: Stohl et al. 2012 ACP Fukushima Xe-133 Cs-137
full_citation: Stohl A., Seibert P., Wotawa G., Arnold D., Burkhart J.F., Eckhardt S., Tapia C., Vargas A., Yasunari T.J. (2012). Xenon-133 and caesium-137 releases into the atmosphere from the Fukushima Dai-ichi nuclear power plant: determination of the source term, atmospheric dispersion, and deposition. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 12: 2313-2343.
notes: Abstract read: Xe-133 15.3 EBq (12.2-18.3), Cs-137 36.6 PBq (20.1-53.1), Xe-133 above the plant inventory estimate (attributed to I-133 decay). Inverse-modelling estimate, higher than UNSCEAR 2013; used only for the high bound of E013.

short_cite: Ruhl et al. 2009 Kingston ES&T
full_citation: Ruhl L., Vengosh A., Dwyer G.S., Hsu-Kim H., Deonarine A., Bergin M., Kravchenko J. (2009). Survey of the potential environmental and health impacts in the immediate aftermath of the coal ash spill in Kingston, Tennessee. Environmental Science & Technology 43(16): 6326-6333.
notes: Read through a summarising fetch. Gives 4.1 million m3 ash and TVA/TDEC mean Ra-226 4.4 +/- 1.0 and Ra-228 3.1 +/- 0.4 pCi/g (n = 12); no bulk density and no tonnage. Used as the ash activity coefficient for all ash events.

short_cite: US EPA Kingston project closeout fact sheet (Dec 2014)
full_citation: US EPA Region 4 (2014). TVA Kingston Fossil Plant ash release: project closeout fact sheet, December 2014.
notes: Read via summarising fetch. 3,500,000 cubic yards removed from the Emory River (Phase 1); 4,000,000 tons shipped to the Alabama landfill; used to derive 1.36 t/m3 (assumes tons are short tons and that the two figures describe the same ash; the sheet does not say so).

short_cite: US EPA Kingston ash release overview
full_citation: US EPA (continuing). TVA Kingston Fossil Plant coal ash release (site overview page).
notes: States approx. 5.4 million cubic yards of coal ash released, covering about 300 acres beyond the storage areas. No tonnage and no radionuclide data. Year of page uncertain.

short_cite: ATSDR Martin County coal slurry health consultation
full_citation: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry. Health Consultation: Martin County coal slurry release, Martin County, Kentucky (file MartinCountyCoalSlurryHC080706).
notes: Read via summarising fetch. About 300 million gallons slurry, 11 October 2000, impoundment south of Inez. Year inferred from the file name (080706); no solids fraction; radionuclides not discussed.

short_cite: USGS CERC ORDA Dan River case page
full_citation: US Geological Survey, Columbia Environmental Research Center, Office of Restoration and Damage Assessment. Dan River Coal Ash Spill (case ID 984).
notes: Date 2 February 2014; about 39,000 tons of ash and 27 million gallons of ash-pond water; Duke Energy Dan River Steam Station, Eden NC. Units "tons" taken as short tons.

short_cite: WFAE 2014 Duke revised Dan River estimate
full_citation: WFAE (2014-02-12). New Duke estimate shows less ash spilled into Dan River.
notes: News report: Duke revised from up to 82,000 tons to 30,000-39,000 tons ash plus 27 million gallons water; leak sealed on a Saturday (taken as 8 February 2014).

short_cite: WNA Tokaimura criticality accident 1999
full_citation: World Nuclear Association (continuing). Tokaimura criticality accident 1999 (information library).
notes: Only quantified release found: about 160 TBq noble gases and 2 TBq gaseous iodine, "apparently released", INES 4. No primary table (Japan NSC, JAERI, IAEA) located; try the Japanese Nuclear Safety Commission accident investigation report (2000).

short_cite: McQuillan (NMED) Church Rock spill table
full_citation: McQuillan D. (New Mexico Environment Department) (2017). Presentation D1_08, 2017 Animas River Symposium, New Mexico Water Resources Research Institute.
notes: Slide table with the 1979 spill row: 94 million gal, pH 1.4-1.9, 1.5 (t U; 1,100 MT tailings), U 4.5-6.4 mg/L, Ra total 210 pCi/L, 46 (gross alpha, Ci). Text extraction garbled the column alignment; the 46 Ci reading is an inference and must be checked on the original slide.

short_cite: OECD-NEA Chernobyl assessment ch. 2
full_citation: OECD Nuclear Energy Agency (2002). Chernobyl: Assessment of Radiological and Health Impact, 2002 update of Chernobyl: Ten Years On, Chapter II: the accident and the release.
notes: Table of core inventory and release (PBq) by nuclide; sum of listed values about 10.9 EBq with Xe-133 (my arithmetic, omits I-133 and Te-129m). Lists Np-239 as about 95 PBq against a 3.5 % release of 27,000 PBq = 945 PBq (typo in source). Used for the low bound of E004.

short_cite: IAEA Bulletin 1996 One decade after Chernobyl
full_citation: Crick M. (1996). One decade after Chernobyl: the basis for decisions. IAEA Bulletin 38(3): 14-23.
notes: Total release about 12 x 10^18 Bq including 6-7 x 10^18 Bq noble gases; I-131 1.3-1.8 EBq. Independent cross-check of E004. Author and title read from the fetch summary.

short_cite: ASN Cahiers Histoire 1 (2024)
full_citation: Autorite de surete nucleaire (2024). Les cahiers Histoire de l'ASN no. 1 (English edition), pages on Saint-Laurent 1969 and 1980 and Lucens 1969.
notes: Saint-Laurent A1 1969 (about 50 kg fuel melted) and A2 1980 (about 20 kg), both INES 4; 1980 discharges stayed below authorised limits; no environmental release quantity given for either. Lucens 1969 described as INES 4 on the /6 page, most activity retained in the cavern. Basis for rejecting these three.

short_cite: Bellona Leningrad NPP 1975 accident
full_citation: Bellona Foundation. Article on the November 1975 accident at Leningrad NPP unit 1 (page ?p=9852).
notes: "Varying estimates" 137,000 to 1.5 million Ci fell on the surroundings; no sources, evidence level low. Year of page not captured. Basis for deferring Leningrad 1975 (not in events.csv).

short_cite: CCNR Chalk River accidents
full_citation: Canadian Coalition for Nuclear Responsibility. Reactor accidents at Chalk River (page ?p=1085), citing Accidents Do Happen.
notes: NRX 1952: "thousands of curies" of fission products to atmosphere, no figure given; NRU 1958 no quantity. Advocacy source, year of page not captured. Basis for deferring Chalk River.

short_cite: Conley et al. 2016 Aliso Canyon methane
full_citation: Conley S., Franco G., Faloona I., Blake D.R., Peischl J., Ryerson T.B. (2016). Methane emissions from the 2015 Aliso Canyon blowout in Los Angeles, CA. Science 351(6279): 1317-1320.
notes: 97,100 t methane released. Used in the bounding calculation that rejects a gas-blowout radon event.

short_cite: Down To Earth Sasan ash dyke breach
full_citation: Down To Earth (2020-04-11). Fly ash dyke breach in Singrauli points to a bigger problem of fly ash disposal.
notes: Sasan (Reliance) dyke breach 10 April 2020; two deaths; slurry spread about 6 km; no volume. Basis for deferring (volume unknown). The Indian National Green Tribunal OA 148/2020 filings may hold a volume.

short_cite: SANDRP Singrauli ash dam breach
full_citation: South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (2020-04-12). Singrauli fly ash dam breach: who regulates these dams in India?
notes: Confirms the date and that no volume was reported; lists earlier Singrauli breaches (Essar August 2019, Vindhyachal October 2019) without volumes.

short_cite: Utility Dive Hurricane Florence Sutton ash
full_citation: Utility Dive (2018-09-17). Hurricane Florence triggers coal ash spill, cuts power to millions.
notes: Duke reported more than 2,000 cubic yards of ash released at Sutton; no other Duke releases reported. Basis for rejecting the Hurricane Florence releases (about 1,500 m3).

short_cite: Water Online Blacktail Creek spill
full_citation: Water Online. Cleanup update following North Dakota's biggest produced water spill.
notes: Nearly 3 million US gallons (EPA report) from Summit Midstream, detected January 2015, Marmon ND. Consistent with S0322 (about 11 million L). Used for the oil and gas rejection.

short_cite: WNA Kyrgyzstan uranium country profile
full_citation: World Nuclear Association (continuing). Uranium and nuclear power in Kyrgyzstan (country profile).
notes: Mailuu-Suu: more than 9,000 tU produced 1946-1967 by the Western Mining and Chemical Combine; 23 tailings dams holding about 1.9 million m3; no mention of a 1958 failure. Purpose of the output (Soviet weapons programme) is not stated on the page; the military classification used for the rejection is my inference (D16 pre-1965 rule).

short_cite: BC Government Mount Polley key information
full_citation: Government of British Columbia. Mount Polley Mine tailings dam breach: key information (past spill incidents).
notes: Failure 4 August 2014; about 17 million m3 water and 8 million m3 tailings and other materials into Polley Lake, Hazeltine Creek and Quesnel Lake. Copper-gold mine (Imperial Metals).

short_cite: ASDSO Feijao Dam B-I case study
full_citation: Association of State Dam Safety Officials. Case study: Feijao Dam B-I, Brazil, 2019.
notes: 9.7 million m3 of liquefied iron-ore tailings released; 272 deaths; failure by flow liquefaction. WISE gives 12 million m3.

short_cite: BHP Samarco update 8 January 2016
full_citation: BHP (2016-01-08). Update: Samarco (60-day update).
notes: About 32 million m3 of tailings released by Fundao (satellite assessment); about 85 % retained within 85 km; early estimates exceeded 50 million m3. Company statement.

short_cite: NMED Church Rock mill site review
full_citation: New Mexico Environment Department. Church Rock mill site review (former uranium mines and mills).
notes: 1,100 tons of tailings and 94 million gallons released, July 1979. No activity totals. Year of page not captured.

short_cite: NRC letter on Sequoyah Fuels UF6 accident 1986
full_citation: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Letter on the 4 January 1986 UF6 cylinder rupture, Sequoyah Fuels Corporation, Gore, Oklahoma (ADAMS ML20029C423).
notes: Qualitative only: cylinder ruptured when heated, one death from HF, public advised to evacuate. Release quantities are in NUREG-1189 Vol. 1, not retrieved. The rejection of this candidate rests on a bounding calculation (cylinder capacity), not on this letter.

short_cite: NRC document on Tokaimura accident (ML003706945)
full_citation: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (2000). Document on the Tokaimura criticality accident (ADAMS ML003706945).
notes: Noble gases and iodine released, environmental levels low; fission count about 2.5 x 10^18 as extracted (exponent possibly garbled); no release quantities. Title not captured; supports the order of magnitude only.

short_cite: IAEA 1999 Tokaimura fact-finding mission report
full_citation: International Atomic Energy Agency (1999). Report on the Preliminary Fact Finding Mission Following the Accident at the Nuclear Fuel Processing Facility in Tokaimura, Japan. IAEA, Vienna.
notes: Read via summarising fetch. 5e17-5e18 fissions (JAERI, preliminary); no release total; only trace amounts of noble gases and gaseous iodine escaped the building; I-131 exhaust maximum about 2.7e-5 Bq/cm3 (OCR uncertain).

short_cite: UN Chernobyl Forum 2006 via GreenFacts digest
full_citation: UN Chernobyl Forum (2006). Chernobyl's Legacy: Health, Environmental and Socio-Economic Impacts (summary as digested by GreenFacts, Level 2).
notes: Total release about 14 EBq (Section 3 and Annex 7), read through a digest, not the Forum report itself (try https://www-pub.iaea.org/MTCD/Publications/PDF/Pub1239_web.pdf). Used as the high bound of E004.

short_cite: Cross 1980 Chalk River NRX accident 1952
full_citation: Cross W.G. (1980). The Chalk River Accident in 1952. Atomic Energy of Canada Limited, Chalk River Nuclear Laboratories; oral presentation, Health Physics Society annual meeting, Seattle, July 1980 (library ID PAM/0089/1980).
notes: Read via summarising fetch. 8,000-30,000 Ci fresh fission products from the 200-ft stack (film-badge based); about 1 million gallons with about 10,000 Ci long-lived fission products pumped to ground disposal. Cited for the Chalk River candidate (not in events.csv).
